title: New Line keeps its other fields, their order and its three buttons
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in to staging (app.staging.shopview.com) as a user with the Admin role (Settings, then Roles & Permissions describes it as "Full system access": every permission is on). Work at the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919: its name shows in the location box at the top right, next to your initials. Other people may change it, so check it before each test; to change it, click that box, then the location name under Change Location, then Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Create an open work order for this test, work order 1, so a saved line can be added to it: go to Work Orders and click Create Work Order: pick a Customer (for example 4 Star Truck Repair) and an asset under Add Asset (for example 2015 Ford Escape), then click Save; if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create. The new work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line window already open; close that New Line window with its X.
  • Have a canned line, canned line A, at Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (click the location box at the top right, then Settings, then Canned Lines under SERVICE in the left menu; for example "Replace - Torque rod").
  • Make sure Require Approval for New Lines is on (Settings, then the Work Orders tab, then Save Settings), so the New Line window shows its Line Approved tick box.
  • Start on work order 1, on its Lines tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click New Line.
  2. Type the first three letters of canned line A's name.
  3. Click canned line A in the list.
  4. Click Save & Close.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Line window opens over work order 1.
  • From top to bottom it shows: the AI SHOPCOACH LINE BUILDER link, Title, Description, Technicians with Add Technician, Labor Rate, Estimated Time and Tech Time, then the Line Approved tick box just above the buttons.
  • The buttons at the bottom are Save & Add Part, Save & Add Line and Save & Close.
  • Only the first two field names (Title and Description) and their grey prompts are new; nothing is added, removed or moved.

Step 2:

  • Canned line A is offered in the list.

Step 3:

  • The window fills in canned line A's title and description.

Step 4:

  • The window closes and work order 1's Lines tab lists a new line with canned line A's title and description, exactly as the canned line holds them.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 17 (28 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 4 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10130 (Story 1, The Work Order Line Dialog)

  • S1-R7: “Nothing else about the dialog changes, other than the label position in S1-R3: same fields in the same order, same validation, same values saved.”
  • S1-R3: “The Title box carries the placeholder "What are you doing?" and the Description box carries "Why are you doing it?". Placeholder text shows while the box is empty and disappears as soon as there is a value. The labels Title and Description always sit at the top of their boxes, empty or filled, with the placeholder underneath; in production the label sat inside the empty box. This is the one layout change in the dialog.”
  • Feature Overview, Core functionality: “Nothing about the values changes: same fields, same storage, same customer documents.”

From: Chris Ward, answer 15 in the Doc "What/Why (Title and Description) – questions for Chris Ward" (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QcT7FRZci6AhYcI33HUac-Oob03-gCnCOKn2NFHMLjA), answered after 28 Oct 2026, read 4 Nov 2026

  • Answer 15: “Yes, keep the "Line Approved" tick box as it is today. It's an existing control that shows when "Require Approval for New Lines" is on, and S1-R7 keeps everything else in the dialog unchanged. The design just doesn't draw it. Not a defect.”

Not yet checked against a build since the 4 Nov 2026 change (the Line Approved tick box).
